selection_review.decision: No exact Bone Riders artwork was found or approved. The strongest fictional cannibal rider source uses a monstrous pig/Manswine rather than a horse and carries melee weapons, while horse-barding sources are riderless, undead, diagrammatic, or lack a sling and ammunition pouch. No cleaned input exists.

strongest_near_miss.title: Slaughter Chief on Manswine, Man Eaters
strongest_near_miss.reason: Bestiarum explicitly presents a living Man Eater rider with crude bone/skull armor on a coherent mounted creature. The mount is visibly a monstrous pig/Manswine, not a living four-legged horse, and the rider has a mace/cleaver-like melee weapon rather than a sling or visible stone pouch. It cannot be converted into a horse or ranged slinger by cleanup or prompt.

search_conclusion: No exact Bone Riders source exists in the defensible archive. The search covered modern game and production art, tabletop and miniature catalogs, professional fantasy/horror portfolios, horse skull/bone barding, mounted slingers, stone pouches, and related character-art queries. Results were dominated by undead mounts, spear/lance cavalry, generic cavalry, riderless armor sheets, wrong mounts including pigs and big cats, culturally anchored imagery, or isolated components. The mandatory single-image combination of living horse, bone barding, living painted feral cannibal rider, visible sling, visible stone pouch, readable tack/four-leg anatomy, and no spear/lance/sword was not found.
